method: Independent direct visual inspection of every final PNG; compared with the earlier desktop/mobile open screenshots and the original Tea Tree reference poster. No browser operation or model/code edit.

observations: Pump stays assembled on the round-shouldered bottle; bottle and refill pouch remain empty.
Navy bottle and pouch labels carry the expected two separate artwork sets.
Product silhouettes and interface controls fit the viewport without clipping.
The complete pump, ivory mechanism and long clear dip tube rise together.
Blank label substrates and printed artwork separate progressively; the bottle and refill remain visible.
The transitional print layer can project across the clear bottle while opening; there is no separate head/stem/closure explosion.
Both blank navy labels occupy the upper label row; both complete lettering sets occupy a separate lower row.
The earlier appearance of refill text belonging to the wrong navy label is removed.
The entire raised pump and tube fit above the open bottle, with visible clearance between the tube end and bottle mouth.
Bottle 750 mL and pouch REFILL artwork are distinct and remain inside the visible scene.
Pump, tube and bottle remain continuous and inside the frame after rotation.
The refill pouch and lettering surfaces are nearly edge-on, so their plane-like projection becomes thin and the artwork becomes difficult to see.
This side-view disappearance is the existing consequence of viewing thin artwork planes edge-on, not an introduced mesh or texture loss.
Both the bottle and refill pouch are fully framed in the simulated mobile viewport.
The assembled navy pump and both artwork layouts remain identifiable.
Product microcopy is small at this viewport width; structure and overall label layout are visible.
The earlier refill-lettering-over-navy-label projection is resolved: navy substrates sit above the separate lettering row.
The two lettering sets remain distinct, complete in layout, and within the scene frame.
The complete pump and clear tube rise together above the bottle, and the refill pouch remains visible.
Microcopy is still small at the simulated mobile size; this is suitable for the overall structure view rather than close reading of printed label details.

resolvedFinding.issue: At the previous full-open pose the refill lettering projected across another navy label, especially on mobile.
resolvedFinding.resolution: Final label Y +0.65 and print Y -1.6 place blank substrates above the complete lettering row. Final desktop-open and mobile-open screenshots confirm the overlap is removed.

scopeChecks: Five customer-facing component groups remain visible in the interface.
Complete pump lifts as one connected assembly.
Empty bottle and refill remain distinguishable.
Blank labels and their lettering are separate; lettering remains farther forward.
Final closed, half-open, fully open and rotated desktop states fit their screenshots.

nonblockingLimitations.detail: At the supplied 393-pixel-wide simulated mobile screenshot, printed label microcopy is small. The two text layouts are complete and separated, but this is not a claim of comfortable close reading at that size.
At a near-90-degree side view, planar artwork and the thin pouch become edge-on and partially disappear. This is existing behavior and not an introduced regression.

The transparent dip tube remains subtle against the grey-blue background, especially on mobile; its long continuous silhouette is visible, and the independent geometry report confirms its thicker hollow wall.

notChecked: New browser interactions by this independent reviewer
Physical packaging or pump engineering tolerances
